source.title: Computationally Informed Insights Into Anhedonia and Treatment by Kappa Opioid Receptor Antagonism
source.venue: Biological Psychiatry: Cognitive Neuroscience and Neuroimaging

confidence_rationale: Theory-driven secondary analysis of a KOR-antagonist RCT plus three other datasets, fitting a resource-bounded reinforcement-learning model that decomposes behaviour into memory and efficiency components, and a perseveration term. The striking result for REE: KOR antagonism increases reward sensitivity AND perseveration, and anhedonia is linked to deviation from OPTIMAL perseveration. This is the most architecturally-specific anchor for the layer's commitment-entropy framing -- 'perseveration' is the closest empirical analogue to MECH-048's commitment-stability construct. Confidence mid-range: secondary analysis, modest KOR n (24/31), and 'perseveration' is an operational proxy for, not identical to, REE 'commitment entropy'.
failure_signatures: The modelling finds KOR antagonism has DISTINCT cognitive effects, only one of which is related to anhedonia -- so the kappa->commitment-stability link is real but partial, and the layer's clean 'kappa = the commitment-entropy axis' framing risks over-attributing a multi-component drug effect to a single axis.

Optimal perseveration is bounded by memory capacity; 'more perseveration' is only therapeutic up to the resource-rational optimum, so a naive 'kappa antagonism stabilises commitment' reading omits the optimality constraint.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Fitting a resource-bounded reinforcement-learning model to Probabilistic Reward Task behaviour (KOR-antagonist RCT secondary analysis, n=24 KOR / n=31 placebo, plus three other datasets), anhedonia was associated with deficits in EFFICIENCY (not memory), arising from an inability to perseverate OPTIMALLY for a given memory capacity; KOR antagonism (likely elevating tonic dopamine) increased both memory and efficiency, which the model attributes to increased reward sensitivity AND increased perseveration.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the closest empirical instantiation of the layer's commitment-entropy axis. MECH-048 frames mu-opioid as a commitment STABILISER that reduces the urge to switch; the layer frames kappa as the destabiliser raising policy entropy. 'Perseveration' in the resource-rational model IS commitment-to-an-action / resistance-to-switching, and 'deviation from optimal perseveration' is exactly the policy-instability the layer maps to pathological kappa drive. KOR antagonism restoring optimal perseveration = normalising kappa-driven commitment-destabilisation -- the PHARM-018 / ARC-086 prediction, in computational-psychiatry terms.
mapping.mapping_caveat: 'Perseveration' is an operational RL proxy, not identical to REE 'commitment entropy'; the optimum is bounded by memory capacity (more perseveration is only good up to the resource-rational optimum), a constraint the REE framing omits. KOR antagonism's effect is multi-component (the paper explicitly says only ONE of its cognitive effects relates to anhedonia), so attributing it wholly to a single commitment-entropy axis over-simplifies. Secondary analysis, modest KOR n.
mapping.source_context: Human; computational (resource-bounded RL) secondary analysis of a KOR-antagonist RCT + 3 additional datasets; Probabilistic Reward Task.

confidence_components.notes: Strong theory-driven analysis from leading computational-psychiatry and KOR groups. Mapping_fidelity is the HIGHEST in strand 3 for the commitment-entropy construct specifically -- perseveration is a near-analogue of commitment stability. Limiters: secondary analysis, modest n, proxy-not-identity, optimality constraint. Transfer risk low (human).
